source_title: Del Monte Foods Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After a Ransomware Attack Exposes Social Security Numbers
source_excerpt:
National class action law firm offers free, confidential case evaluations to individuals whose personal information may have been exposed in the Del Monte Foods data breach.
NEWTOWN, Pa. , Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Edelson Lechtzin LLP , a national class action law firm, is investigating data privacy claims arising from a data breach at Del Monte Foods Corp. II Inc., an American food production and distribution company headquartered in Walnut Creek, California. Anyone who received a breach notice or believes their information may have been exposed can request a free case evaluation .
On February 9, 2026, Del Monte Foods detected an issue affecting its network operability and began an investigation with independent cybersecurity experts. The investigation determined that unauthorized parties acquired certain files from the company's systems, and on or about August 20, 2026, Del Monte learned the compromised data contained personal information. The breach reportedly occurred on February 7, 2026.
On March 31, 2026, while the investigation was underway, a ransomware group known as Payouts King claimed responsibility for the attack on the dark web, saying it had obtained about 1.2 terabytes of Del Monte's internal data. Del Monte disclosed the incident to the Attorneys General of California, Massachusetts, and Vermont on October 29, 2026, and began notifying affected consumers in late October 2026. The company has said it implemented enhanced security measures and is cooperating with law enforcement.
According to Del Monte Foods, the personal information involved may include:
Because Social Security numbers, financial account information, and health records are among the most sensitive categories of personal information, the exposure creates a heightened risk of identity theft and financial fraud for affected individuals.
The investigation focuses on individuals whose personal information Del Monte Foods maintained and who are receiving breach notification letters. Del Monte is offering affected individuals complimentary identity protection services through Kroll, using the unique enrollment code included in each notification letter before the stated deadline.
Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating a potential class action on behalf of individuals whose data may have been compromised. A successful case could recover compensation for losses such as lost time, out-of-pocket costs, and loss of privacy, and could press Del Monte Foods to strengthen its data protection. The firm evaluates claims at no cost.
Watch for the notice from Del Monte Foods and keep the enclosed enrollment code for the complimentary identity protection services being offered.
Place a free fraud alert or credit freeze with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, and obtain your free reports at AnnualCreditReport.com.
Review your bank, card, and insurance statements for anything you do not recognize, and report suspected identity theft to the Federal Trade Commission at IdentityTheft.gov.
Speak confidentially with a data privacy attorney: Marc Edelson, Esq., Edelson Lechtzin LLP , 411 S. State Street, Suite N-300, Newtown, PA 18940; Phone: 844-696-7492 ; Email: [email protected] ; or click HERE to request a free consultation.
Edelson Lechtzin LLP is a national class action law firm with offices in Pennsylvania and California. Beyond data breach litigation, the firm handles class and collective actions involving securities and investment fraud , antitrust violations, ERISA benefit plans, wage theft , and consumer fraud .
